obligation: Covered telecommunications or video surveillance equipment report
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d)(1)-(2) (Section 889), flowed down under 52.204-25(e); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Owner identifies covered equipment (Huawei, ZTE, Hytera, Hikvision, Dahua, or their subsidiaries or affiliates, including white-label units) used as a substantial or essential component of any system during performance, or is told of it by a supplier or other source
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (contract number, order numbers, supplier, brand, model, item description, mitigation); further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: The prime's subcontracts manager, as the BPA states; the prime reports to DoD through https://dibnet.dod.mil
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - FAR 52.204-25 is in the prime's BPA

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c)(1)-(2); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Owner identifies a Kaspersky Lab covered article provided to the Government during performance, or is told of it by a supplier or other source
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification; further information within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: The prime's subcontracts manager, as the BPA states (DoD reports go through https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - FAR 52.204-23 is in the prime's BPA

obligation: Suspected counterfeit or nonconforming item delivered to the prime
trigger: A suspected counterfeit, tampered, or nonconforming item was delivered on, or is staged for, the prime's orders
Becoming aware or having reason to suspect that an item purchased for delivery to the Government is counterfeit or suspect counterfeit
deadline: Within 60 days: written notice to the contracting officer and a GIDEP report; keep the items until disposition instructions
applies_at_this_tier: No - not in the BPA. Check each new purchase order from the prime for this clause

obligation: DFARS cyber incident report affecting covered defense information
trigger: Cyber incident affecting covered defense information on a covered contractor information system
notify: DoD (DIBNet portal); subcontractors also notify the prime
applies_at_this_tier: No - the BPA has no DFARS 252.204-7012 clause and the owner holds no CUI. If the prime ever adds the clause or sends CUI, re-scope first (POL-01 8.3)

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents (for example a user name or email address with a password, or a name with a financial account number and access code). A sole proprietorship is a covered entity (501.171(1))
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
applies_at_this_tier: Unlikely - the business holds little personal information (business contacts only). Check with counsel if a mailbox or SYS-01 takeover exposed any personal information

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business holds personal information of far fewer than 500 individuals

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the business (inbound)
trigger: A vendor that maintains personal information for the business (accounting SaaS, email provider) has a breach of security
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days following the determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - inbound; watch for vendor notices

citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of state residents (definitions vary by state)
deadline: Varies by state (for example 'without unreasonable delay' or a fixed number of days)
notify: Affected residents; state attorney general or regulator where the state requires it; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Always check. Customers are in Florida; apply the law of each state where any affected resident lives

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom or extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware or extortion payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if an extortion demand is made. All U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

obligation: Business email compromise and payment fraud report
trigger: A supplier or company mailbox is used to request a payment or bank change, whether or not money moved
deadline: Voluntary; file as soon as possible and call the bank fraud desk at once to try to recall any payment

citation: Business owner's policy, data breach endorsement (contract)
notify: Insurance agent and carrier claims line
applies_at_this_tier: Only for a data breach ($25,000 sublimit). Funds transfer fraud and counterfeit stock are not covered

obligation: Form 8-K Item 1.05 material cybersecurity incident disclosure
trigger: Public company determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within four business days after determining the incident is material
applies_at_this_tier: No - the business is not publicly traded

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident / ransom payment reports (pending final rule)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment by a covered entity (as defined in the final rule)
deadline: 72 hours (covered incident); 24 hours (ransom payment) - not yet effective
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; recheck when final
